transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we finalize the flag settings. While tracing a separate permissions bug yesterday, I found that 23 legacy admin endpoints update permissions without emitting the invalidation event that the new cache consumes. I've been confirming which endpoints still use that path, which is why I haven't filed the adapter work yet. I believe the rollout plan must include a binding commitment to build and verify an invalidation adapter for those 23 endpoints before we expand beyond the initial cohort.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share the results from my load rehearsal this morning before we finalize anything. The rehearsal measured invalidation-queue propagation at a 9-minute p95, and the queue stays within its safe operating limit only when the first rollout cohort is capped at 10 percent. Additionally, for this rollout the authorization cache lifetime must be set to exactly 300 seconds. I haven't updated the rollout ticket yet because the rehearsal finished after the change-control review began, so this data isn't in the ticket.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share a finding from a support-case review I completed recently. All 11 SCIM-managed enterprise accounts use an admin workflow that cannot yet explain delayed permission changes. These accounts must be excluded from the first rollout cohort, and a support playbook must be prepared before they are enabled. I hadn't posted this yet because the cases were being reassigned between support queues at the time.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Build and verify an invalidation adapter for the 23 legacy admin endpoints before expanding rollout beyond the initial 10 percent cohort.
Update the rollout ticket with the load rehearsal results showing 9-minute p95 invalidation-queue propagation and the 10 percent cohort cap.
Prepare a support playbook for delayed permission changes before SCIM-managed enterprise accounts are enabled in any rollout cohort.
Maintain a revocation kill switch as a required operating safeguard for the rollout, enabling immediate rollback if invalidation issues surface in production.
